subject: Rerank/Embeddings follow-up & next tests (vs Hyperscalers)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@datasearch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rerank/Embeddings follow-up & next tests (vs Hyperscalers)

Thanks for the time today, Samantha — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call summary:
- Use case: customer-facing search + recommendations where reranking top-K from an initial retrieval matters.
- Current evals: you mentioned internal runs against Bedrock and Vertex for embedding quality.
- Key success criteria you highlighted: retrieval latency <= 50ms (P95), recall@10 >= 0.85, and cost per 1K embeddings under $0.50.

How Redwood differentiates (short):
- Latency-focused runtime with KV cache + continuous batching to keep P95 inference tight for retrieval-style traffic.
- Lightweight rerank models we ship for hybrid pipelines and guidance on vector dims vs recall/cost tradeoffs.
- Transparent unit economics + tooling to simulate production throughput and predict cost at scale.

Proposed next tests: (we can run these or support you to run)
1) Embedding quality sweep: compare recall@k (k=1,5,10) on your sample dataset across 3 vector dims (128, 256, 768) vs your Bedrock baseline.
2) Retrieval latency: synthetic replay at target QPS to measure P50/P95/P99 and cold vs warm (cache primed) behavior.
3) Cost estimate: per-1k embedding and per-query rerank cost at three throughput points (10/s, 100/s, 500/s).
4) Rerank accuracy: run NDCG@10 and recall@10 for our recommended small reranker vs your current production reranker.

What we need from you to start:
- A representative sample dataset (1000 queries + ground-truth for recall/NDCG) OR permission for Redwood to run a synthetic evaluation using your schema.
- Confirmation on whether we should include AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex as comparison points (you said Bedrock + Vertex today).

Deliverables & timeline (estimate):
- 5 business days to run a full sweep if we have your sample set + access (or 3 days for a synthetic run).
- Deliver a short report with recall@k, latency percentiles, cost per 1k embeddings, and recommended vector dim + reranker config.

I've attached a quick KPI matrix to capture the test plan and an initial trial agreement for procurement.

Next step: can you share the sample dataset or let us schedule a short call to hand off the data? Happy to set up a dedicated trial environment if you want more control over the tests.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Rerank/Embeddings follow-up & next tests (vs Hyperscalers)

Thanks, Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Yes, please include Bedrock (we're using Anthropic/Claude embeddings there) and Vertex in the comparison. We also have a month-old run against an internal FAISS setup.
2) The recall@10 >= 0.85 baseline is non-negotiable for product.
3) For latency, our target is P95 < 50ms for the rerank step (we can accept higher end-to-end times if the initial retrieval is async) — can Redwood show warm vs cold behavior?
4) On vector dims: our current embeddings are 1024d for some models; we are open to dim reduction if recall holds. Cost target: total embedding cost (if we were to re-embed our corpus nightly) should stay below $0.50 per 1k (we understand ballpark).

We can share a 1k-query sample with ground truth by EOD tomorrow. Procurement copied for the trial agreement redlines; they'll follow up if needed.

Also, can Redwood provide an SLA/uptime note for any dedicated trial infra? We may want to test a dedicated instance if performance is materially better.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Search Engineering | DataSearch Inc.
samantha@datasearch.com

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Samantha — that works. 

Responses inline: 
- We'll include Bedrock and Vertex in the sweep plus a FAISS baseline if you can share the embeddings or a sample snapshot.
- We'll report warm vs cold latency; our benchmark harness captures cache priming and steady-state.
- Vector dims: we'll test 128/256/768 and also run a 1024d config if you provide a sample so you can see the compression tradeoffs.
- Dedicated trial infra: we can spin up a short-term dedicated pool (1–2 GPUs) for the tests; SLA for trial is not enterprise SLA but we'll commit to availability windows and a point-of-contact (SE).

Next steps:
- Please upload the 1k sample + ground truth to the Drive folder I shared (or reply with a link).
- Procurement: happy to take redlines; copying Marissa (CS lead) and Stephanie (Solutions Eng).

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow for handoff and to define the exact metrics. Shall I send a calendar invite?

Thanks,
Aditya
